headers._comment: Security headers apply to EVERY response, including client-side routes such as /login and /dashboard. Firebase rewrites those to /index.html, so scoping these headers to '/index.html' alone silently skips them. Cache-Control is deliberately absent here; the rules below own caching.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://apis.google.com https://www.gstatic.com; connect-src 'self' https://*.googleapis.com https://securetoken.googleapis.com https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com https://firestore.googleapis.com https://firebaseinstallations.googleapis.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; frame-src 'self' https://*.firebaseapp.com; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests

headers._comment: Document and client-side route responses must never be cached, so a deploy takes effect immediately on a hard refresh.
Static media copied from public/ is not content-hashed, so it gets a week rather than a year.
Everything Vite emits into /assets is content-hashed, so it can be cached immutably for a year. Listed last so it wins over the rule above for the same header.
